Signs: a single toll, resonance through the deck, pressure waves that crack hulls. People believe it is calling Nyara; Atlantean wardens track how close its tolls come to the Throat.

lore.title: Black Trawl
lore.text: Black Trawl: great apex of the margins of the Sea of the Ghost Fleet; treat as EG10: divert or flee. Signs: fishing fleets gone overnight, nets hauled up full of nothing, a darkness under the water wider than a harbor. People believe it feeds the Ghost Fleet.

lore.title: Southern Coil
lore.text: Southern Coil: great apex of the southern rainforest's rivers; treat as EG10: divert or flee. Signs: rivers changing course overnight, scales as big as doors found on the banks, villages moved because the river moved. Some elves say the rivers follow it.

lore.title: Pale Orbit
lore.text: Pale Orbit: great apex of the sky above the Hollow Aurora Zone in the far north; treat as EG10: divert or flee. Sign: a pale light circling the northern sky; patrols that walk out under it never return. Northern clans say it watches the Deep Northern Apex and will not travel when it is overhead.

lore.title: Grey Walker
lore.text: Grey Walker: great apex of the ashlands around the Wailing Battlefield; treat as EG10: divert or flee. Sign: a grey figure walking slowly; where it passes, the dead lie still and do not rise again. The Ashen Veil hates it, some priests pray to it, the Church denies it exists. No account ties it to Nareth.

lore.title: Vaulkir the Pale Maw
lore.text: Vaulkir the Pale Maw: apex direwolf of the Glass Howl Icefield in the Deep Northern Apex, a white wolf the size of a hill leading packs that hunt in whiteouts; divert or flee. Its howl cracks the ice. When its packs reach the tundra edge, the White-Horn Clans move their herds and the Frostbound prepare for war.

lore.title: Coasts and Seas
lore.text:
- Outlines are approximate; settlements and recorded routes stay authoritative. Coasts are charted only in the south, east and southwest.
- East coast (Emerald Sea): the mainland shore runs south past Lanternshoal, around Marisk Bay (Marisk on its western shore, Tidesong Isle across its mouth) and past Vargate; south of Corrowen it curves southwest past the Sea of the Ghost Fleet to the southern cape. The Tidebound archipelago lies offshore.
- Barak Gulf: opens east between Vargate and Corrowen and runs about 1,200 km west to Barak Freeport, where the Belis River enters. North shore: Highmark, the Chieftainate shore at Hurrakai, the Coastway. South shore: Southmarch and Saelmark.
- Saltreach: narrow tidal firth, 20-50 km wide, from the Emerald Sea west to the Grand Vein's estuary at Saltledger Quay, with Marshledger and Pearlbank near its head. Rainhoof Crossing at its narrows is a tidal ford where herds cross at low water.
- Southern Deep: open ocean south of the cape. From the cape the coast runs west past the rainforest, north along the Western Sea to Saltglass Harbor (Ashkaran port), then west into uncharted land; the Long Passage follows it. Beyond the outer seas: the Unknown Reaches.

lore.title: Islands of the Emerald Sea
lore.text:
- The Tidebound Covenant is an archipelago; its towns are on islands unless named mainland (Lanternshoal is a mainland lighthouse town). The Stormmere Isles lie across a strait of about 80 km from the mainland; Tidesong Isle faces the mainland across the mouth of Marisk Bay.
- Atlantis lies undersea in its dome; the Abyssal Throat is a black-rock atoll. The Island of Lost Time and the Nameless Isle, at the heart of the Sea of the Ghost Fleet, are restricted.

lore.title: Forests
lore.text:
- Southern Rainforest: hot, wet jungle along the southern coast, home of the Southern Coil's rivers and the Fairy Court's giant canopy.
- Verdantleaf Forest: the elven forest; the Fairy Court lies beyond its southern edge.
- Thornheart: deep forest between Ardelia and Verdantleaf; the Root-Tyrant's range.
- Elenvar Oldwood: old forest around Elenvar, Ardelia.
- Witchwood: the Witch's misted forest in the Dragonfang's eastern foothills.
- Greypine Forest: northern pinewoods above the Border Kingdoms and Valegard, watched from Furuvord.
- Frostbound Taiga: cold forest north of the belt, hunting grounds of the Frostbound and the White-Horn herds; only its southern edge is charted.

lore.title: Mountains and Highlands
lore.text:
- Dragonfang Mountains: the great range enclosing the Ironanvil Holds, dragon heights in the north. Windcutter Pass carries the Ironanvil Mountain Road through its eastern wall and closes for weeks in deep winter, months in a hard winter. The Stone That Walks shifts its inner passes.
- Ardelian Highlands: dry, windy uplands cut by green river valleys.
- Kessel Peaks: high country around Dornhald and Kesselheim.
- Saltspine Ridge: low broken ridge in the northern Western Barrens.

lore.title: Rivers, Lakes and Marshes
lore.text:
- Grand Vein: flows east from Black Iron Riverhold via Thousand Sails to Saltledger Quay and the Saltreach.
- Ledger River: from Thousand Sails north via Coinwater and the lock towns to Ledgerford; the Upper Ledger takes barges on north to the last lock at Frostgate. It flows south, so northbound is upstream.
- Bluewatch Branch: flows south from hills north of Bluewatch to Glassdock; the run to Bluewatch is upstream.
- Marrow River: from the Dragonfang foothills east past the Holy City, then south past Highmark Capital into the Barak Gulf; fast, shallow, small boats only.
- Ulf River: from the Greypine hills through Lake Dunmere's outflow south-east to the Ledger at Reedmere; rafts and small boats only.
- Eastern floodplain channels, east of the Ledger: shallow-draft boats only.
- Belis River: from Belisar north to the Barak Gulf at Barak Freeport.
- Lakes: Mirror Lake (Verdantleaf), Lake Dunmere, Tarnby Water, Oathmere (Highmark). Marshes: Sorrowfen (about 150 km across), Gallowsmere, Rosefen, Reedmere.

lore.title: Plains, Barrens and Wastes
lore.text:
- Chieftain Plains: grassland, mesas and herd country of the Chieftainates, south of the Saltreach. Whistlegrass Steppe: open steppe north of it.
- Western Barrens: gravel plateaus, dry valleys, salt flats, old battlefields.
- Glass Wastes: fused-glass desert, the Glass Crown's range. Ashkaran Desert: arid basin and oases from there to the Western Sea.
- Iron-Blue Tundra and the Apex Ice: frozen apex lands of the deep north.

lore.title: Uncharted Lands
lore.text:
- Uncharted North: between the taiga's charted edge (~y 215) and the apex lands (~y 470). Expeditions cross it to the Deep Northern Apex and disagree on what lies between.
- Uncharted West: beyond the Ashkaran Dominion, west of ~x -290, north of the Western Sea shore. Ashkaran caravans and slavers know its edges; no one has charted it.
- Uncharted Northwest: beyond the Western Barrens and north of Ashkaran, west of ~x -140 and north of y 60.
- Uncharted Northeast: north and east of the mainland coast above ~y 130.
- Uncharted Southwest: west of Verdantleaf and the Kessel Peaks, south of the Ashkaran Dominion, behind the southern and western coasts. Long Passage ships sight it, never land; no road crosses it.
- Unknown Reaches: beyond the Western Sea, the far Emerald Sea and the Southern Deep; no coordinates, nothing canon until play makes it so.
- Uncharted is not empty: places may be generated in play like any unmapped space, kept once named, recorded in the story; but no major route or crossing is invented through them.

lore.title: Route Query Rules
lore.text:
- Distances, route codes and paces come from the pack's recorded routes. Follow only connected routes, reversing as needed; junctions and straight-line proximity add none.
- Give slow and fast bounds; never average or pick the fastest. Only an established mount, vessel, species, spell or relic replaces ordinary pace, for that method alone; level never raises travel speed or bypasses access.
- Modes: no wagons on trails, mountain roads, tunnels or hidden ways, and riders keep foot pace there. Deep sea only with Atlantean pressure craft or escort. Flight only if sustained flight is established in play; no one sells flights. The Long Passage takes months.
- Delay only from an established complication (weather, season, mud, locks, customs, patrols, damage, permits, convoy size), combined once, never stacked. Moving within one settlement takes minutes or hours, never travel days.
- A route grants no vessel, mount, guide, permit, key, supplies, weather window or access. A route to a Wildzone, dungeon or special site proves access, never ownership; crossing a border never merges jurisdiction.
- Campaign events may change a route's usability, never create shortcuts or move geometry. Auvoth to the Glass Howl and Barak to Greenveil are always staged seasonal expeditions.
- Km and paces are GM metadata; NPCs speak in travel days, stages, landmarks and rough estimates.

lore.title: Callings: the Twelve Lines
lore.text:
Everyone starts Awakened: Level 1, no school. People are then known by the training they took, each a ladder of three titles an institution confers after years of real work. A title says where someone trained, never their level.
- Soldier: Man-at-Arms, Iron Guard Sergeant, Iron Guard Knight (Highmark's Iron Guard Academy).
- Shield: Hall Shieldbearer, Hammerfall Oathshield, Hammerfall Holdfast (the dwarven shield halls).
- Duellist: House Fencer, House Duellist, Judicial Champion (the Mirage City houses).
- Pit fighter: Pit Hand, Knifeglass Gladiator, Pit Champion (Shackles).
- Breath monk: Breath Disciple, Snowbell Monk, Snowbell Breath Master (Kvildal).
- Hunter: Lodge Tracker, Longstride Hunter, Lodge Huntmaster (the Chieftainates).
- Assassin: Stalker, Shadow Blade, Executor (Hand of Oblivion).
- Thief: Infiltrator, Phantom, Grand Redistributor (Nightingale).
- Mage: Spell Student, Journeyman Spellwright, Startrace Master (spell grammar).
- Runecarver: Rune Apprentice, Oathvault Runecarver, Rune Master (Ironanvil).
- Priest: Acolyte, Flame Cleric, Inquest Flamecaller (the Church).
- Healer: Hospice Novice, Hospice Healer, Grove Healer (temples, hospices, the Grove Schools).
Other callings exist in the same spirit; name them from the institution that teaches them.

lore.title: Sir Volkmar
lore.text: Sir Volkmar, 'the Old Stone', a champion of the Wardens of the Last Wall: a grey giant famous for never giving ground in a shield line. He wants a young knight worth teaching and a place in the line when it matters, and fears the Order growing soft. Wardens swear by him.

lore.title: Council Speaker Aaltje Brouwer
lore.text: Aaltje Brouwer, Council Speaker of the River Confederacy this term: a banker's daughter from Ledgerford, neat and soft-voiced, ink on her cuffs. She wants the rivers open and Highmark's debt honored, and fears a default. Merchants trust her arithmetic; the frontier doubts she has seen mud.

lore.title: Duke Evert of Shorn
lore.text: Duke Evert of Shorn rules Shornmarch from the frontier bastion at Shorn: a bluff, weather-cracked man who knows his village headmen by name. He wants Council money for his forts, and fears the Turning and Highmark troops on the Auvoth road. His hill folk love him; the Council thinks him a beggar.

lore.title: High Pontiff Gratian
lore.text: Gratian, 'Ember-Keeper', High Pontiff of the Church of the Eternal Flame and sovereign of the Dominion: a broad, serene old man in ash-grey vestments. An Expansionist, he blesses the Reopening, wants kings who enforce burial law, and fears the Flame's authority slipping. The faithful adore him.

lore.title: Conclave Elder Clementia
lore.text: Conclave Elder Clementia, leading voice of the Restorationists in the Conclave of Embers: a spare, silver-haired woman who speaks softly. She holds that the Reopening courts another Abyssal Tide and fears being dismissed as gloomy. The pious respect her; the Expansionists wait her out.

lore.title: Grand Commander Vitus
lore.text: Grand Commander Vitus of Silvermark leads the Order of the Silver Mark: a heavy, square-jawed man in plate, with a pilgrim's worn boots. He wants the burial roads safe and the Veil's cells burned, and fears undeath outrunning his knights. Pilgrims bless him; he is first called when the dead rise.

lore.title: King Constantin of Ashmere
lore.text: King Constantin of Ashmere, the Church's closest royal ally: a stout, pious man with candle-wax on his sleeves. He wants his crown's sacred legitimacy and his candle, relic and funerary trades rich, and fears royal law losing to Church doctrine. Pilgrims love him; his nobles mutter.

lore.title: Duchess Tove of Valegard
lore.text: Duchess Tove of Valegard rules the buffer duchy: a lean horsewoman who still rides her own border herds in all weather. She wants her herds and crossings safe and her cavalry unspent, and fears Highmark's succession quarrel. The horse-lords obey her; envoys find her polite and immovable.

lore.title: King Torleif of Redspire
lore.text: King Torleif of Redspire holds the Border Kingdoms' rotating council chair: a grey-bearded king in a patched winter cloak who counts beacons, not courtiers. He wants the warning chain lit and no kingdom left alone, and fears being bought piecemeal by Highmark. The Long Watch trusts him.

lore.title: Thane-of-Thanes Dagny Hearthslag
lore.text: Thane-of-Thanes Dagny Hearthslag speaks for the Ironanvil Holds at the Council Beneath Stone: a short dwarf with iron rings in her braid and forearms thick as hammer-hafts. She wants grain, timber and salt for the Holds, and fears a hold leaving. Every crown courts her steel.

lore.title: Elder Bodvar Runecutter
lore.text: Elder Bodvar Runecutter, a stooped Ironanvil elder with rune-scarred fingers who teaches young runecarvers. He wants the old craft passed on, and fears it dying with its teachers. Secret (only a few elders share it): he can read the Iron Archive's script, and no crown is told.

lore.title: Sea-Lord Merrit Capstan
lore.text: Sea-Lord Merrit Capstan speaks for the Tidal Council at Abysswatch: a barrel-chested admiral with a voice like rope on timber. He wants the convoys running and the sea lanes open, and fears a war at sea the Covenant cannot afford. Captains call him fair; Atlantean pilots call him stubborn.

lore.title: The Sea God Witch Marenthe
lore.text: The Sea God Witch Marenthe, Atlantis's highest spiritual authority: a pale, still woman who weighs every word. Her foresight is fallible, and Atlanteans know it. She wants the wards kept and the deep's counsel kept. Secret (no one else knows): she has dreamed of the north going white.

lore.title: Tide-Archon Ondaris
lore.text: Tide-Archon Ondaris chairs Atlantis's governing council: a tall, formal Sea Folk noble whose speech is slow and exact. He wants the wards intact and the Sheathless at arm's length, and fears surface troubles reaching the dome. Nobles call him prudent; surface envoys call him a locked door.

lore.title: Emperor Liutmar
lore.text: Emperor Liutmar of Rhunwald, Ardelia's elected emperor, serving his fixed 18-year term, which ends in July 612: a heavy, patient man in a plain cloak. He wants the electors' law honored and his term to end quietly, and fears the Knights of the Last Day. The electors respect him; citizens call him a steady hand.

lore.title: Arch-Chancellor Gerlinde
lore.text: Arch-Chancellor Gerlinde, chosen by the electors for life, keeps Ardelia's laws and seals: a spare, grey woman who reads every document twice. She wants the Constitution obeyed to the letter, and fears any bloc bending it. The electors respect her; citizens barely know her face.

lore.title: Saelwyn, Voice of the Elder Root
lore.text: Saelwyn, Voice of the Elder Root, interprets the Verdantleaf Elder Root: an elf in moss-grey robes who pauses long before answering, as if listening. She wants the old treaties kept and the forest's boundary closed, and fears the Reopening reaching it. Outsiders find her courteous and immovable.

lore.title: Foxglove-at-Noon
lore.text: Foxglove-at-Noon, Queen of Flowers, rules the Fairy Court from the high canopy: a small fairy with foxglove-purple wings, seen only in full daylight. She wants her court hidden and her people safe from collectors and binders. The elves protect her; most of the world takes her for a tale.

lore.title: High Chieftain Oshadai Spear-Wall
lore.text: High Chieftain Oshadai Spear-Wall speaks for the Chieftain Council at Battle Cry City: a broad beastfolk with a spear-scarred shield arm and a slow voice. He wants clan honor kept and slavers off clan land, and fears Vargate's slave ships. Clans call him fair; foreign armies call his scouts dear.

lore.title: The Glass Regent Daryush-ul-Mirrorwell
lore.text: The Glass Regent Daryush-ul-Mirrorwell rules Ashkaran from Ashkar as the Glass Crown's steward: a lean man in mirrored glass-steel thread who receives petitioners before the Regent's Mirror. He wants slaves for the pits and the Crown content. Merchants court him; slaves know him as rumor.

lore.title: Frost Queen Eydis Long-Winter
lore.text: Frost Queen Eydis Long-Winter leads the Frostbound from a moving war-seat: a tall, weathered woman in white fox and froststeel. She wants her people fed and their oaths kept, and fears winters that grow harsher each year. Her warbands trust her; southern border villages dread her name.

lore.title: Ketil Ice-Oar
lore.text: Ketil Ice-Oar, Frostbound champion, famous for raids in bad winters: a hulking man with frost-blackened fingers who fights with a long, ice-pitted oar. He wants plunder and a saga worth singing, and fears a hungry winter. Border villagers bar their doors at his name.

lore.title: Herd-Mother Ylva of Hornwake
lore.text: Herd-Mother Ylva of Hornwake, senior voice of the White-Horn Clans: an old woman in sheepskin who rides a great mammoth and reads the sky for Long Thunder's storms. She wants the herds fed and the clans together, and fears hard winters. Riders obey her; traders buy her wool.

lore.title: Seal-Captain Gurda Kelthul
lore.text: Seal-Captain Gurda Kelthul, dwarf captain of the Order of the Sealwardens: square-built, in lamp-blackened mail, she checks every ward twice. She wants every warden home from a shift and the seals unbroken, and fears a breach with too few lamps. Recruits fear her; adventurers owe her.

lore.title: Sunniva Halvard
lore.text: Sunniva Halvard, 'the Lantern of Auvoth', a living S-rank Spellwright: a slight woman who keeps a small steady light about her even in daylight, and whose barrier-work is said to hold a Depths gate alone. She wants her juniors alive and fears being needed everywhere. Auvoth sends for her first.

lore.title: Kaidu Thrice-Returned
lore.text: Kaidu Thrice-Returned, a living S-rank beastfolk Hunter who came back from three 'certain death' contracts: lean and quiet, a cord of three knots at his wrist. He scouts the northern wildzone for the Guild and trusts his eyes over any map. Juniors tell his stories; he never corrects them.

lore.title: Pell Underhay
lore.text: Pell Underhay, 'the Smallest Legend', a living S-rank halfling infiltrator: cheerful, round-faced, with quick hands and a habit of being somewhere else. He wants a fat purse and no one's leash, and fears owing too many people. He is said to owe the Nightingale and take work from rival crowns.

lore.title: The Ninth Brazier
lore.text: The Ninth Brazier, an A-rank party of four working the northern wildzone out of Bluewatch and Auvoth. Their banner is a brazier on a black field. They want S-rank contracts and a name that outlives the job board, and fear a job above their letter. Bluewatch likes them; rivals watch their picks.

lore.title: First Marshal Adelind Corbel
lore.text: First Marshal Adelind Corbel, elected head of the Wallwright League: a tall, practical woman in a leather apron over her armor, hands crossed with mortar scars. She wants the League's walls held and charter fees paid, and fears a war of conquest. Every crown wants her engineers.

lore.title: The Sparrow
lore.text: The Sparrow is the Nightingale's public face and voice, out of Shackles' Mute Sparrow Ward: a soft-spoken, cheerful figure in a plain grey hood. The title passes on; the current Sparrow's real name is unknown. The Sparrow trades war secrets to every side and never robs the dead.

lore.title: Ottavia Vane
lore.text: Ottavia Vane, 'the Phantom of Vargate', the Nightingale's champion and the best Phantom alive: slim, forgettable, dressed as whatever the room expects. She has stolen from three crowns and returned one theft to make a point. She wants a theft worth a legend and fears boredom.

lore.title: The Key-Widow
lore.text: The Key-Widow is a Broken Chain legend, said to wear on a black ribbon the key of every collar she has opened. No one agrees whether she is real, one woman, or only a title. Slaves whisper her name; slave-factors deny she exists, and the Chain's cells neither confirm nor deny it.

lore.title: Neshai Chainbreaker
lore.text: Neshai Chainbreaker, the Broken Chain's champion: a beastfolk fighter, once a pit slave, who breaks rune-collars with her bare hands. Old collar-scars ring her neck. She wants every collar broken and fears recapture. Slaves tell her story in the dark; Shackles and Vargate pay for her head.

lore.title: Warmother Vashka
lore.text: Warmother Vashka leads the Cinder Host, chosen in war: a grey-streaked, hard-eyed commander who wears a burnt ledger page as a sash. She wants plunder for her people and chains broken, and fears a real army turning west. The Northern Belt calls her horde-queen; her followers, Warmother.

lore.title: Grusk the Ledger-Burner
lore.text: Grusk the Ledger-Burner, the Cinder Host's champion: a huge, soot-streaked orc who has burned eleven debt registers and the clerks guarding them. He wants more registers to burn and fears only being left behind by his Host. Barrens towns bar their record rooms when he comes.

lore.title: Saintess Velka
lore.text: Saintess Velka, 'Keeper of Names', the Ashen Veil's counter-saint, revered by the cells that keep the dead: a small woman in grey who whispers the names she has kept. Secret (her followers do not know): she holds the oldest Veil cells' proof against the Church, and profits from the northern dead.

lore.title: Saltbone Ide
lore.text: Saltbone Ide, notorious Ashen Veil cell leader and the Veil's champion in the field: a lean, salt-rimed man who smells of brine and old smoke. He wants stolen remains and a Veil ward in every port, and fears the Silver Mark. The Church names him heretic; the Inquest wants him.

lore.title: The Quiet Hour
lore.text: 'The Quiet Hour' is the Hand of Oblivion's most famous Executor. No description agrees: a man, a woman, a child's voice on a stair. The Hand never says whether it is one Executor or several. Targets are said to notice the room go quiet first; great houses double their guards at the name.

lore.title: Teodor 'Nine Collars' Vask
lore.text: Teodor 'Nine Collars' Vask, Shackles' pit champion of the Ironhammer Brotherhood, has won and lost his freedom nine times: a massive, scarred man with nine iron rings at his belt. He wants a tenth freedom that holds, and fights for whoever buys him. The pit crowds adore him.

lore.title: Captain Sorrel of the Ninth Debt
lore.text: Captain Sorrel of the Ninth Debt, collared captain of the Grey Ledger's debt-slave company: a lean veteran with a keyed collar and a captain's whistle, who knows every name in the company. She wants her soldiers' debts worked off, and fears the Ledger's next reckoning.

lore.title: Captain Murrough of the Gallowglass
lore.text: Captain Murrough of the Gallowglass, Bloodbound captain who holds a line past all reason: a bearded, battered man on a long axe, who lifts his helm only to drink. He wants the contract kept and each dead soldier's share paid to kin, and fears breaking faith. Employers hire him for bridges.

lore.title: Startrace's Northern Tap
lore.text:
Startrace keeps leyline-tapping records it denies having: how the First Abyssal Tide began, the tapping and the warnings before it. They never name the primordial; the records do not know it.
In CY 610 Master Albrecht Somner led a Startrace expedition up the Hollow Aurora route with forty condemned prisoners bought from Highmark, to feed a leyline tap with their deaths; they tapped the leyline under the Pale Orbit's light. The tap is still open and growing, and it is the cause of the Third Abyssal Tide. Somner has not written since; whether he lives is unknown. Closing the tap is the one known way to stop the Tide at its source; no one knows how, and Veyr's sealing records in Auvoth are the best hope. The Archmaster will deny the expedition until proof is laid before the Compact Council.

lore.title: The Emperor's Chamber
lore.text: Emperor Adalmar died last winter. What sits in the furs is a pattern held together by Veil necromancy, wearing his face: it can sit, nod and sign, and says almost nothing. Wendhild ordered it to buy time until the Diet would ratify her. Up close it is wrong: no warmth, no breath on cold mornings, a smell the incense covers; a Listener would hear a death frequency, not a living soul. When it fails or is completed, the Emperor's death is announced as if new.

lore.title: Atlantean Customs
lore.text: Atlantis arranges its marriages by bloodline, and the elder families keep the lists. A Sea Folk who runs from a match shames the house; the family hires retrievers, patient hunters who bring runaways home, alive and quietly. Sharing breath with a Sheathless, taking a land-dweller down under your own sheath, is forbidden: whoever does it is struck from the rolls, and the dome is closed to them for good. Pilots who serve surface captains are tolerated because the Tidebound needs them, and watched because of it.

lore.title: The Lamp-Thief of Vargate
lore.text: Vargate's children have a ghost story: the lamp-thief, who walks the rich wards on rainy nights and puts out their bound lamps one at a time. Ward-lords pay watchmen to sit up with their lamps; the lamps go dark anyway. Bound lamps hold small spirits sealed in glass, and they burn for generations. Nobody has caught the thief. Poor families sometimes find candles left on the step.

lore.title: Trade Goods
lore.text: Markets reckon goods in six kinds. Food: grain, flour, bread, salt fish, dried meat. Fodder: hay, oats. Arms: blades, arrows, armour, steel. Mounts: horses, mules. Medicine: herbs, bandages, healing draughts. Drink: ale, wine, spirits. Frontier towns pay more for bread and bandages; grain country, river towns, horse plains and mining towns sell their own goods cheap at the source. War, famine, sickness and clipped coin change prices, and every trader knows which.

lore.title: After the Last Wall
lore.text: After the Last Wall the north is a new frontier. The line runs south of Bluewatch now; refugee clans settle the empty farms behind it under Guild charters, and the Guild rules from Shorn as much as from Auvoth. Signal towers are rebuilt further south. Far north, past the snow, travellers swear a single lamp still burns.

scores.name: Tide Pressure
scores.means: How strong and how far south the Third Abyssal Tide has come. Raised by Tide stages and by neglect; lowered only by striking at its cause.

scores.name: North Readiness
scores.means: How prepared the north is to meet the Tide: seals held, forts manned, refugees fed, warnings believed.

scores.name: Highmark Stability
scores.means: How firmly Highmark holds together: a ratified ruler, paid armies, a quiet Diet.

scores.name: Highmark Coin
scores.means: Trust in Highmark's silver, the continent's common coin. Debasement lowers it; a recoinage restores it.

conditions.name: harvest-failed
conditions.means: The harvest failed here; stores will not last the winter.

conditions.name: grain-dear
conditions.means: Bread and fodder cost far more than usual; the poor go hungry.

conditions.name: plenty
conditions.means: A good harvest is in; markets are full and bread is cheap.

conditions.name: refugees
conditions.means: Columns of refugees fill the roads and camp at the walls; food runs short and tempers shorter.

conditions.name: at-war
conditions.means: The realm is at war; levies march, roads fill with soldiers, steel and horses are scarce.

conditions.name: garrisons-away
conditions.means: The realm's soldiers are away on campaign; forts and roads at home are thinly held.

conditions.name: court-divided
conditions.means: Claimants court the Diet, borrow and buy swords; officials hedge and every favour has a price.

conditions.name: crown-contested
conditions.means: No ruler is ratified; claimants gather swords and votes, and officials hedge.

conditions.name: regency
conditions.means: A regent rules in the heir's name; nobody is sure how long it will hold.

conditions.name: slaves-pressed
conditions.means: Slaves and bondsmen are driven to war works and fortifications in numbers; the Chain stirs.

conditions.name: siege
conditions.means: The place is besieged: gates shut, food rationed, every wall manned.

conditions.name: raiders
conditions.means: Raiders strike farms, caravans and border posts; travellers move in armed company.

conditions.name: coin-debased
conditions.means: Highmark's silver is clipped; merchants weigh every coin, prices climb and wages buy less.

conditions.name: tolls-raised
conditions.means: Tolls are raised against Highmark goods; barges queue at the locks and smugglers prosper.

conditions.name: unrest
conditions.means: Crowds are angry and the watch is nervous; a spark could start a riot.

conditions.name: debt-called-in
conditions.means: Lenders call in their debts; families sell land, tools and themselves into bondage.

conditions.name: inquest-active
conditions.means: The Church Inquest is here; lay healers are questioned, informers are paid, and people watch their words.

conditions.name: plague
conditions.means: Sickness spreads; towns post cordons, healers are overwhelmed, and travellers are turned back.

conditions.name: dead-uncompleted
conditions.means: The dead are rising here: death has gathered past what the land can hold; graves stir, and nobody walks the fields at night.

conditions.name: roads-closed
conditions.means: The route is closed: washed out, snowed in, held by an enemy or cordoned.

conditions.name: blockade
conditions.means: Warships or privateers hold the lane; only the desperate and the well-paid sail it.

conditions.name: wildzone-pushing
conditions.means: Front ladder step 1: low-band beasts spill onto roads and farms near the wild edge; farms empty out.

conditions.name: stampede
conditions.means: Wildzone herds are on the move; frontier roads are deadly and signal towers burn day and night.

conditions.name: dungeon-unworked
conditions.means: Too few delvers work this dungeon; what lives below grows bold and spills toward the surface.

conditions.name: guild-stretched
conditions.means: The Guild cannot fill its contracts; bounties rise and it takes whoever signs.

conditions.name: tide-touched
conditions.means: Front ladder step 2: the Tide has reached this land; frost out of season, deeper-band beasts and elites, packs led by something worse.

conditions.name: wild-breaking
conditions.means: Front ladder step 3: apex signs; things that should never leave the deep wild walk the roads.

conditions.name: festival
conditions.means: A feast, fair or holy day fills the place with crowds, music and spending.

conditions.name: burned
conditions.means: The place was burned; survivors camp in the ashes and rebuild slowly.

conditions.name: evacuated
conditions.means: The place has been abandoned in an evacuation; only scavengers and the stubborn remain.

conditions.name: fallen
conditions.means: The place has fallen to an enemy or the Tide; its people are dead or fled.

markets.note: Everything comes up the road; beast parts are cheap, bread and bandages are not.
Grain country: bread, flour and hay are cheap at the source.
Barges bring grain and salt fish down every river.
Horse country: mounts and fodder are cheap.
Iron and steel are at hand; blades and armour cost less.
Temple healers sell herbs and draughts; pilgrims drink.
Water and fodder are dear; caravans name the price.
The far north grows nothing; everything is carried in.

templates.summary: People come home to {place} and open the shutters again.
Something climbs out of {place} that nobody has seen above ground in years.
A power makes a move in {place}.
Someone in {region} reaches for what they want.
